narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Slightly cooler and clearer than yesterday; winds little changed. Largely dry, with thunder possible, peaking this evening. 29°C (85°F) high, 19°C (66°F) low. Sky clear early as reported, partly cloudy at midday and mostly cloudy in the evening. Wind NNE early and SSW at midday; gusts to 38 km/h (21 kt). UV index 9.2 (very high). Air quality 68 (moderate), by the CAMS model. As of 06:01, reports through 05:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 20°C (68°F); low so far 19°C (66°F); peak sustained 7 km/h (4 kt); sky clear.

## Extended Outlook

Temperatures and winds much the same through Tuesday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Skies mostly cloudy Sunday, then partly cloudy Monday and mostly cloudy Tuesday. Tuesday's call: rain, 100%, with all four models wet; highs 27 to 30°C (81 to 86°F). Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls it wet. At this lead Best Match has the best record, right 90% of the time over 84 checks.

Further out, cooling through Saturday, with rain and thunderstorms likely Wednesday and Thursday, rain possible Friday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Saturday. Wednesday: all four models wet, highs 25 to 29°C (77 to 84°F). Thursday: all four models wet, highs 24 to 27°C (74 to 81°F). Friday: all three models that reach it wet, the week's wettest day at 26 mm (1.00 in) on average, highs 19 to 25°C (66 to 76°F), no thunder.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Thursday. GFS is the wetter solution from Wednesday to Thursday; ECMWF, ICON and UKMO keep it drier. Saturday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 25°C (76°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 90% of the time over 80 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Convective instability in the hours ahead: UKMO 8600 J/kg, ICON 1990 J/kg, ECMWF 1560 J/kg and GFS 610 J/kg. Thunder likely; any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above the 38 km/h (21 kt) forecast.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Peak gust 31 km/h (17 kt). Any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above this figure; the water is unsafe while one is nearby.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1007 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1013 hPa) — a 6 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is filling over the next three days. Pressure overhead is rising. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across the basin's 5 points, pressure today sits between 1012.2 and 1014.2 hPa, rising by 2.7 hPa over three days. Pressure here over the last 24 hours: +1.9 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

On rain the record ranks Best Match first at Day+3, right 90% of the last 30 checks and ECMWF first at Day+7, right 90% of the last 30 checks. On today's high UKMO is the warmest model at 30.4°C (86.7°F) and ECMWF the coolest at 29.1°C (84.4°F); the call's 29.4°C (84.9°F) sits between them. Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls a high of 28.0°C (82.4°F) and rain, agreeing with the call on rain. At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet. At Day+7, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and GFS the weakest. At Day+0, Best Match slightly under-forecasts daytime highs here.

Figures issued 06:01. Written by code; a discussion follows when a model answers.
